title: RBAC, Audit Logging, Data Residency, Secure SDLC, and Incident Response — Controls & Evidence Workflows
author: Sophia Harris
body:
Overview:

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's controls and operational workflows for: role-based access control (RBAC) and authentication, audit logging and log retention, data residency and retention requirements, Secure Software Development Lifecycle (Secure SDLC) controls, incident response for security events, compliance evidence collection workflows, and risk/exception management. It describes owners, thresholds, and concrete steps to generate evidence for audits.

Purpose and scope:
- Provide a single reference for security controls applied across Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
- Define operational workflows for producing compliance evidence (SOC/ISO/GDPR) and approving risk exceptions.
- Audience: security engineers, SRE, platform, legal, and compliance auditors.

1) RBAC & Authentication

Summary:
- All access to internal services, console, and control plane APIs must be authenticated via the centralized identity platform (Identity Service: auth-service + policy-engine).
- RBAC is implemented through the policy-engine using named roles and attribute-based constraints for sensitive resources.

Key roles and owners:
- Identity & Access Management (IAM) service: eng-infra (owner: eng-infra-team@redwood.com)
- Policy authoring and review: security (owner: security@redwood.com)
- Console and control plane access: product (owner: product-ops@redwood.com)

Roles and privileges (examples):
- admin: full control over control plane, reserved for security and platform engineering (max 8 accounts).
- infra-ops: deploy and manage infra; no access to customer data by default.
- service-account: least-privilege keys scoped to a single service / namespace.
- analyst: read-only access to logs and dashboards (PII redaction applied).

Controls and standards:
- All human access requires SSO with MFA (FIDO2 + TOTP fallback).
- Service accounts require short-lived tokens (<= 24h) obtained via the token service and signed by KMS.
- Role changes must be requested via the access request portal and approved by the resource owner; automated approvals allowed only for predefined workflows.
- Quarterly access reviews (owner: security) with automated certification emails to resource owners.

Audit guidance for RBAC:
- Evidence to produce: access control matrix export, access request tickets, MFA enrollment logs, quarterly certification reports.
- CLI sample to export role assignments (example):
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
    https://auth.redwood.internal/api/v1/roles?format=json > rbac_export_$(date +%F).json

2) Audit logging and observability

Logging architecture:
- Services emit structured JSON logs to local log agent (log-shipper) → Kafka (audit-topic) → audit-collector → long-term storage (encrypted) and SIEM (Splunk/Elastic).
- Critical audit events (authn/authz changes, policy updates, administrative actions, cryptographic key usage, data exports) are tagged "audit:critical" and ingested into a protected index with 7-year retention for enterprise customers.

SLOs and thresholds:
- Audit pipeline ingestion latency: 99th percentile <= 30s end-to-end for non-batch events.
- Lost-audit-events threshold: < 0.01% per month. Alerts fire on >0.05% loss.

Retention policy (default):
| Data category | Hosted customers | Dedicated customers | Private deployment (on-prem) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Audit logs (non-sensitive) | 90 days | 1 year | Customer-managed |
| Audit logs (sensitive/regulated) | 1 year | 7 years | Customer-managed |
| Metrics & traces | 30 days (hot), 365 days (cold) | 365 days | Customer-managed |

- Retention can be extended by contract for enterprise accounts; custody and deletion operations are logged and require approval.

Log protection and integrity:
- Logs are signed at write time using the log signing service (logsigner) and stored encrypted with customer/key-specific KMS.
- Immutable retention buckets used for compliance-critical archives.

Evidence collection for audits:
- Export commands: use the audit-collector API to query and export events and verify signatures.
  Example:
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $AUDIT_TOKEN" \
    'https://audit.redwood.internal/api/v1/events?start=2025-01-01T00:00:00Z&end=2025-01-31T23:59:59Z&tag=audit:critical' \
    -o january_critical_audits.json
- Verify signatures using logsigner-cli: verify-signature --manifest january_critical_audits.json

3) Data residency & retention controls

Regional mapping:
- US: us-west-2, us-east-1 regions (default for US customers).
- EU: eu-west-1, eu-central-1 (GDPR-compliant zones).
- APAC: ap-southeast-1 (available for select customers).

Controls:
- Customer data is pinned to the region(s) selected at account creation. Cross-region replication of customer PII is disallowed unless explicit contractual consent is provided.
- Data exports and backups are tagged with residency metadata. Export requests trigger an approval workflow (owner: customer-data-ops).

Retention specifics:
- Default retention for customer-generated artifacts (prompts, completions, embeddings): 90 days for Hosted unless customer opts into longer retention.
- Customers in regulated industries can select 7-year retention and on-request export formats (NDJSON + signed manifest).

Compliance: GDPR & Schrems II considerations:
- EU customer data stored in EU regions by default; transfers use SCCs and documented DPA.
- For international transfers, we maintain records of processing activities and implement additional safeguards (encryption, minimization).

4) Secure SDLC (controls applied across repo lifecycles)

Objective:
- Prevent introduction of security defects, manage third-party risk, and ensure reproducible builds for deployments to production.

Gating controls (pre-merge / pre-release):
1. Static Application Security Testing (SAST) run on all PRs. Block merge if critical severity or >2 high severity findings remain open.
2. Software Composition Analysis (SCA) for dependency vulnerabilities. Block if dependency has a known critical CVE without a mitigation plan.
3. Secrets scanning (pre-commit and CI). Any detected secret triggers incident workflow and immediate token rotation.
4. Mandatory code review from at least one engineer from a different team for security-sensitive services.
5. CI reproducible builds and signed artifacts (build artifacts stored in artifact-repo with immutability).

Runtime protections:
- Canary deploys with automated rollback on error or SLO breach.
- Runtime policy enforcement (WAF/rate-limits) and runtime threat detections (RASP signals to SIEM).

Owner and evidence for audits:
- Evidence: SAST/SCA reports, pull-request review logs, signed build artifacts, deployment manifests, and pre-release security sign-off ticket.
- Responsible: eng-developer-experience (CI pipeline), security (security gating config).

5) Incident response — security procedures

Overview:
- Security incidents are triaged by the security on-call (pager: security-oncall) and follow the Incident Response (IR) playbook. All security incidents generate an "ir-XXXX" incident in the incident tracker and a corresponding runbook.

Severity levels and SLAs:
- Sev-1 (Critical compromise, active data exfiltration): Paging within 5 minutes, containment plan within 30 minutes, executive notif within 1 hour.
- Sev-2 (Service-wide compromise w/ no confirmed exfil): Paging within 15 minutes, containment plan within 2 hours.
- Sev-3 (Local impact / single customer): Notification in Slack channel and ticketing; contain per runbook within 24 hours.

Triage checklist (initial 15 minutes):
1. Confirm and classify (auth, data, infra, supply-chain).
2. Gather telemetry: auth logs, audit logs, network flows, and recent deploy activity.
3. Isolate affected systems (if required).
4. Start forensic capture (disk/image/ram) per forensics runbook.
5. Engage legal/comms for regulatory reporting thresholds (owner: legal@redwood.com).

Forensic evidence preservation:
- Preserve signed audit log slices and snapshots of relevant services. Use the forensic-preserve tool: 
  forensic-preserve --incident ir-XXXX --scope service-bucket --output /evidence/ir-XXXX.tar.gz
- Hash and sign preserved artifacts and store in compliance-evidence-repo with ACLs restricted to incident responders.

6) Compliance evidence workflows (how to prepare for audits)

Artifacts typically required for SOC2/ISO/GDPR audits:
- Policies and evidence: access-control matrix, RBAC exports, MFA logs, vendor assessments.
- Operational evidence: runbooks, incident timelines, retro/postmortems, SLO reports.
- Technical evidence: signed build artifacts, SAST/SCA reports, audit log exports with signatures, key rotation logs.

Standard evidence collection workflow:
1. Create evidence request ticket in compliance-tracker (tag: audit-YYYY).
2. Security sets the scope and assigns owners for each artifact with a deadline.
3. Owners use the compliance-evidence CLI to export artifacts and attach them to the evidence ticket. Example:
   compliance-evidence export --ticket audit-2026-001 --type audit_logs --start 2025-01-01 --end 2025-12-31 --output evidence/audit-2025.zip
4. Evidence is validated by the security reviewer and then uploaded to the secure evidence vault (object store with immutability and restricted ACLs).
5. Auditor access is granted via time-limited signed URLs and recorded in the evidence tracker.

Retention and access controls for evidence store:
- Evidence vault retention: minimum 7 years for compliance engagements.
- Access to vault is restricted to security, legal, and named auditors. All accesses are logged and auditable.

7) Risk management and exceptions

Exception process:
1. Submit a Risk Exception Request (RER) via the risk portal with: owner, scope, compensating controls, estimated duration, and remediation plan.
2. Security performs risk assessment (likelihood/impact) and assigns risk rating (Low/Medium/High).
3. High-risk exceptions require approval from CISO and CFO; medium-risk exceptions tabled for quarterly risk committee review.
4. Exceptions have an expiration date and automated reminders; they must be re-reviewed before expiry.

Compensating controls examples:
- Network isolation + flow logs when full encryption at rest is not immediately feasible.
- Additional monitoring and shorter rotation windows for keys not in HSM.

Audit trail for exceptions:
- All RERs are stored in the risk register. Evidence for an approved exception includes acceptance emails, compensating control configs, and periodic review notes.

Appendices

A. Contacts and ownership:
- Security leadership: security@redwood.com
- SOC & Incident Response: soc@redwood.com, security-oncall@pager.redwood.com
- IAM / Access: eng-infra-team@redwood.com
- Compliance evidence vault owner: compliance-evidence@redwood.com

B. Useful commands and quick references:
- RBAC export: 
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
    https://auth.redwood.internal/api/v1/roles?format=json > /tmp/rbac_export.json
- Audit export: 
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $AUDIT_TOKEN" \
    'https://audit.redwood.internal/api/v1/events?start=2025-01-01T00:00:00Z&end=2025-01-31T23:59:59Z' \
    -o /tmp/january_audits.json
- Forensic preserve: forensic-preserve --incident ir-XXXX --scope service-bucket --output /evidence/ir-XXXX.tar.gz
